topic: Exact Filter-Before-Top-K vs Naive Oversampling Failure in Collaborative Filtering
problem_statement: Evaluate recommendation generation architectures to guarantee exact Top-K unseen recommendations for all users, including heavy users with up to 32,200 Train ratings, without fixed-oversampling truncations.
root_cause: Naive oversampling strategies (such as calling recommend(K) and then dropping seen items) return fewer than K items or empty lists when the user's top-predicted items have already been watched in Train.
solution_or_decision: Implement Exact Filter-Before-Top-K by setting seen item scores to -inf prior to Top-K selection. Combine with fast 2D argpartition and deterministic tie-breaking (als_score DESC, movieId ASC). Verified to return exact K items for all 162,541 users with 0 seen item leakage.
evidence: Tested against counterexample where naive oversampling returns 0 items while exact filter-before-top-K returns 5 valid unseen items. Tested on user 72315 with 32,200 seen items; completed in 12.55 ms with 0 leaks.
